headline: X offers $1M in payouts for live streamers, launches new Live Studio
summary: X is incentivizing creators with a $1 million fund to boost live streaming on its platform. A new "Live Studio" command center provides tools for easier broadcasting and stream management.
details: X is allocating $1 million to incentivize creators to live stream on its platform, aiming to boost engagement with the feature. This initiative comes alongside the launch of Live Studio, a new command center designed to simplify the live streaming process for creators.

Nikita Bier, X's head of product, announced the $1 million fund, with more details on payout structure to follow. He also demonstrated Live Studio, which offers a comprehensive suite of tools for professional streamers.

Within Live Studio, creators can schedule streams, set titles and thumbnails, and control audience visibility (e.g., verified accounts, subscribers, or public). The command center also provides real-time analytics, showing concurrent viewers, their countries, and devices.

Live streaming on X is currently exclusive to users with an X Premium subscription, costing $3 a month. The platform has faced past challenges with live event stability, including issues during high-profile political announcements.

headline_marked: [[Kimi K2.7 Code now available]] in GitHub Copilot, offering a new open-weight, lower-cost option
headline: Kimi K2.7 Code now available in GitHub Copilot, offering a new open-weight, lower-cost option
summary: This marks the first open-weight model selectable in Copilot's model picker, providing developers with more choice and a potentially lower-cost alternative for their coding workflows.
details: Kimi K2.7 Code, an open-weight model, is now generally available within GitHub Copilot. This marks the first time an open-weight model is offered as a selectable option, providing developers with more flexibility.

The model is billed at provider list pricing under usage-based billing, potentially offering a lower-cost option compared to other models. Users can find detailed pricing information on GitHub Copilot's official page.

Initial rollout is for Copilot Pro, Pro+, and Max plans, where users can select Kimi K2.7 Code in Visual Studio Code. The expansion to Copilot Business, Enterprise, and other surfaces will occur in the coming weeks.
For Copilot Business and Enterprise, Kimi K2.7 Code is off by default. Plan administrators must enable the policy in Copilot settings for their organization to access it.

Administrators are advised to review open-weight models against their security, compliance, and data-governance requirements before enabling them. GitHub provides documentation on supported models to help users choose the right AI for their tasks.
